history.summary: CSV CORRECTIONS: (1) Town is NOT Tirunelveli - the temple stands in the village of Thirupudaimarudur near Veeravanallur, Ambasamudram area. (2) District is Tenkasi, not Tirunelveli (Ambasamudram taluk moved to Tenkasi district in the 2019 bifurcation; many older sources still say Tirunelveli). Documented with the corrected location. The Arulmigu Narumbunathaswamy Temple is an ancient Shiva shrine on the northern bank of the Thamirabarani, revered as 'Dakshina Kasi' - the Kasi of the South. Legend says Munis and Devas sought a Shiva temple equal in merit to Kashi Vishwanath, and Shiva threw his thandam (staff) which travelled upstream of the Thamirabarani to this spot. The sthala vriksham is the Marudha (Arjuna) tree; the place is called Pudarjunam, alongside Srisailam (Mallikarjunam) and Thiruvidaimaruthur (Madhyarjunam). Per the Tamraparni Mahatmyam: Agastya saw the swayambhu linga inside the Arjuna tree; Adhi Manu tried to cut the tree and discovered Mahadeva within; Devendra was relieved of Brahmahathi dosha after bathing at the Tamraparni-Kadana confluence and worshipping Putarjuneshwarar (still celebrated as the Thai Pusya Tirthavari); Karuvur Chithar crossed the flooded Tamraparani on Shiva's word to have darshan. The leaning swayambhu lingam bears marks of deer scratches and a sickle cut. The five-tiered gopuram is famed for its mural paintings (Ramayana, Mahabharata, Periya Puranam, sthala purana, contemporary life) and carved woodwork, attributed to Vijayanagara-Nayak patronage. The temple is the 4th of the Pancha Guru Sthalams (Dakshinamurthy in unusual poses). The precinct's tall trees host painted storks and pelicans.

name: Thirupudaimaruthur Temple
town: Thirupudaimarudur (CSV town 'Tirunelveli' is WRONG - the temple is in the village of Thirupudaimarudur near Veeravanallur, Ambasamudram area)
town_description: Thirupudaimarudur is a small agricultural village on the northern bank of the Thamirabarani river near Veeravanallur in Ambasamudram taluk. Paddy, banana and sugarcane grow on the river's fertile plains, and the temple's tall trees host large numbers of painted storks, pelicans, egrets and herons - an ornithological survey site. The village's history is inseparable from the Narumbunathaswamy Temple.
